Q3 guide revenue $1.90-1.98B, adj EPS $4.33-4.79; Street 4.33; whisper 4.55 (80% 4.24-4.86); our model 5.22. DY has beaten its EPS guide by 13-62% three quarters running, but the industry read-through is mixed-to-negative for the outlook: MasTec's Communications revenue fell 11.8% with backlog -7.5% q/q and customer deferrals in H2 2026, and AT&T cut its 2027-28 capital-investment outlook. The stock is -61% from its high with a sector-wide de-rating (MTZ -56%, FIX -42% from highs), so reversal and continued momentum roughly cancel. I centre the distribution at today's price with a monthly sigma of ~19% (annual 53%/3.5 = 15% widened for the print), no directional tilt. reasoning: Round 2 (after the supervisor): approved driver set restored exactly; my lower comms_ntm_backlog path (-2.9%, 303.83) moved to variants, gap_note and the downside case. Supplier finance confirmed at 367.4 (XBRL) and 196.6 treated as debt-like on the AP-days test (-$6.6/share). SBC now counted once (shares -0.9%/yr from buybacks only, +~$1/share). EV/EBITDA leg rebuilt on LTM GAAP with own EV including supplier finance: 11.0x (k 0.71). Peers: 4 whole-company (MTZ, PWR, PRIM, MYRG) set the 18.65x median; EME, FIX, STRL segment-only; LMB dropped. Guidance records extended to 6 quarters (revenue median +5.0%, 1 miss; EBITDA 6/6 beats, +8.8%) and an FY26 annual period for the segment guides. Model EPS FY27 ~18.3 (Zacks 15.98, SA 17.06), FY28 ~20.2 (18.98 / 20.77), FY29 ~23.4 (22.37): above consensus mostly on H1 beats and Q3 5.22 vs whisper 4.55. Round 1 trace: Industry lane. 1) Why the stock halved: the de-rating is sector-wide (MTZ -56%, FIX -42%, EME -28% from 52-week highs per Twelve Data quotes) and, for DY, the Aug 26 guide (wireless ~$150M deferred to FY28, comms margin slight decline) plus a new low on Oct 20-21, the same day AT&T lowered its long-term capital-investment outlook ($22-23B a year in 2027-28 vs $23-24B in 2026) and a week before MasTec showed Communications revenue -11.8%, margin 6.7%, 18-month backlog -7.5% q/q, with customers deferring H2 2026 spend. Peers with data-center exposure fell on strong prints (FIX book-to-bill ~2), so sentiment ('AI build-out ends next year') is part of it. 2) Chain view of demand: carriers - AT&T still targets 60M fiber locations by 2030 (39M now) partly via a GIP/CPP JV, signed multiyear fiber supply with Corning, and Verizon targets 40-50M passings (32M at YE26) while cutting opex and capex slightly; long-haul - Lumen plans 30M new intercity fiber miles by 2028 and MasTec won 2,100 hyperscaler miles for mid-2027; BEAD - ~$21B after savings, ~63% fiber, construction peaks 2027-2030; data centers - Census put-in-place at a record $96.5B SAAR, hyperscalers guide 2027 capex up, but Microsoft cited third-party data-center delays. Net: volume keeps growing but slower than the approved backlog path, so I cut comms_ntm_backlog growth to ~7%/yr FY28 and ~6% FY29 (worth about -$9/share) and keep the other approved drivers. 3) Valuation: model EPS FY27 ~18.3 (Zacks 15.98, SA 17.06: +7-15%, mostly the beat record already in H1 and Q3 at 5.22 vs whisper 4.55), FY28 ~19.8 (Zacks 18.98 +4%, SA 20.77 -5%), FY29 ~22.4 (Zacks 22.37, in line). Horizon P/E 13.2x from the shrink rule (k=0.8) on a 4-name whole-company peer median of 18.65x; EV/EBITDA 10.9x cross-check. 4) Scenarios move backlog, comms margin and BS share plus the multiple; the downside sits further from base (fat left tail) because customer concentration (AT&T + Verizon 30.5%) and an industry deferral are the visible risks. Research was limited to web search/fetch; X/social sources not used. sec.gov filings were read with WebFetch; no request carried a name or email.

Building Systems revenue: Q4 FY26 95.8 (Power Solutions from 2025-12-23), Q1 FY27 395.4, Q2 FY27 397.5 incl. National Technology Integrators ~22.9 (Q2 FY27 release text; closed 2026-07-02, 10-Q https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/67215/000006721526000043/dy-20260801.htm). Power Solutions alone: CY2024 revenue $736.8M (audited, 8-K/A Ex.99.1 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/67215/000119312526099470/d72789dex991.htm), 9M 2025 $752.1M (Ex.99.2), i.e. ~2.1% of the market in both periods. adjustments.name: Supplier finance program (debt-like part)
adjustments.note: Equity-level, no interest (suppliers bear the discount). 367.4 confirmed obligations at 2026-08-01 (XBRL) of which the payable stretch the program funds is debt-like: AP days 18.8 before the program (223.5/1,084.5x91 at 2025-01-25) vs 27.7 at 2026-08-01 (610.0/2,005.9x91); excess 8.9 days x 2,005.9/91 = 196.6 (53.5%).

downside.story: 10th percentile: my lower backlog path (about -5% vs the approved one by FY29: AT&T 2027-28 capital investment cut to $22-23B a year, MasTec Communications backlog -7.5% q/q with customer deferrals) plus a real carrier program cut at AT&T or Verizon (NTM backlog -14% vs the approved path, book-to-bill under 1); Communications margin -200bp as crews are under-absorbed (MasTec Communications EBITDA margin 6.7%, -460bp y/y) and Verizon/Frontier pricing pressure; data-center electrical slips (BS share -25%, BS margin -300bp as Power Solutions estimate gains reverse); the P/E de-rates 3 turns to ~10x.

upside.story: 90th percentile: the ~$150M deferred wireless and BEAD construction land in FY28 with hyperscaler long-haul awards (Lumen PCF, Corning multi-year optical agreements), NTM backlog +8% vs the approved path, Communications margin +100bp on volume, Building Systems share +15% as 2027 hyperscaler capex rises, and the P/E recovers 3 turns toward the peer median (~16x).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set using Kilian's approved DY set exactly (drivers, quarters, driver_build, years[].shareholder_returns); my lower comms_ntm_backlog path is in variants, gap_note and the downside case only. Supplier finance: 196.6 debt-like as an equity adjustment. No DCF (policy). model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: 1) comms_ntm_backlog: my industry evidence (MasTec Communications backlog -7.5% q/q with deferrals, AT&T 2027-28 capex cut, DY NTM backlog flat Q1->Q2) supports Q3 5,420 / Q4 5,580 / FY28 5,969.3 / FY29 6,323.2 instead of the approved 5,450 / 5,650 / 6,236.5 / 6,684.6: 303.83 (-$9.1, -2.9%).
